match.reason: The bank point 'The cost of borrowing' teaches the same idea (interest, fees and term decide what a loan costs) at a suitable Year 9-10 depth, and its questions are fair for a NSW Stage 5 student, though it does not name personal loans, credit cards or home loans.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-cost-borrowing, covers how interest, fees and term set a loan's cost, but it never covers the ways people borrow (personal loans, credit cards and home loans), so the new point is broader and adding that would be new content rather than a small change.

rejected.title: Borrowing money
card: Borrowing means using someone else's money now and paying it back later, with interest. Interest is the extra amount the borrower pays the lender for the loan.
Personal loan
a set amount borrowed for a purpose such as a car, repaid in regular instalments over a fixed time.
Credit card
a card that lets you borrow up to a limit when you buy things. You are charged interest on any amount you do not repay in time.

A home loan is a large loan to buy property, usually repaid over many years. A loan's real cost depends on its interest rate, fees and term (how long it takes to repay), and at the same rate a longer term means more interest in total.
rejected.remember: A loan costs the amount borrowed plus interest and fees, and a longer term lets more interest build up.

a.q: Which of these is the best description of interest on a loan?
opts: The extra amount paid to the lender for borrowing
The amount borrowed from the lender at the start
A fee paid once to open the loan account
The time the borrower has to repay the loan
a.why: Interest is the extra the borrower pays the lender for using their money. The amount borrowed is not extra, and the time to repay is the term, so those options describe other ideas.
a.clue: Think about what the lender gets on top of being repaid.

b.q: Tariq can repay a $10,000 personal loan over 2 years or 5 years, at the same interest rate and with the same fees. Which statement is correct?
opts: The 5 year term means more interest in total
The 5 year term means less interest in total
Both terms mean the same total interest
The term has no effect on the total interest
b.why: With the same rate and fees, a longer term gives interest more time to be charged on the money still owed, so the total interest is higher. The 5 year repayments are smaller each time, which can make it look cheaper, but it costs more overall.
b.clue: Think about how long money is still owed.
